Commentary.Commentary: Pakistan get into a huddle. Salman Agha seems to be the most animated and he is trying to pump his team up. The umpires walk back out to the middle and Pakistan players disperse. Meanwhile, the openers for Afghanistan - Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Sediqullah Atal are ready to walk out to the middle. As always, Shaheen Afridi will take the new ball. He will look for swing and wickets. Gurbaz to face. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, 142 is the target for Afghanistan to win the final. However, we have to keep in mind that no side has won chasing in this tri-series yet. The key players for them will be Ibrahim Zadran and Sediqullah Atal, who have been in terrific form, but if Pakistan can manage to pick them up early, we will have a game on our hands. Also, if Rahmanullah Gurbaz gets them off to a flier, that would be handy as well. Whatever the result, we are in for an exciting run chase. Stay tuned for the second essay.

Afghanistan's Noor Ahmad is up for a chat with the broadcasters. He says he wanted to just keep it simple, to hit the right lengths and lines. About the wicket, he mentions it looks good and helpful for the spinners if you hit the right lines and lengths. Believes that they will chase this target down, but stresses about batting well in the Powerplay. Expresses his happiness with the way he performed with the ball and says this has been a good preparation for them as a team for the upcoming Asia Cup.

Afghanistan came out fired up for this final, and it showed in their bowling and fielding. Rashid Khan, in his milestone 100th T20I, led from the front with a brilliant three-wicket haul. Their four spinners completely smothered Pakistan, sharing six wickets between them, while Fazalhaq Farooqi backed them up perfectly with two of his own. It was a spirited, all-round effort that set the tone for this big game.

Pakistan just never found their rhythm with the bat. The only real flow came during that 49-run stand between Saim Ayub and Fakhar Zaman, but once that was broken, it was all stop-start cricket. Every time they looked to build momentum, a wicket would fall and pull them back. Salman Agha tried to inject some life into the innings but became a victim of Rashid Khan’s brilliance. In the end, a couple of spirited cameos from Mohammad Nawaz and Faheem Ashraf dragged them to something they can at least fight with.

141 might seem like a below-par score, but the tension of a final does funny things to players. Runs on the board in a game like this are always gold. Still, you have to give Afghanistan huge credit; their bowlers were relentless, and they would’ve gladly grabbed this total with both hands at the start of the night.

Length, wide on off, again, a slower ball. Afridi charges down the track and swings his bat with all his might, across the line of the ball. He is beaten on the inside edge and the ball dribbles back to the keeper. They rush for a bye, and Gurbaz has a shy at the striker's end, but misses. The bowler collects the ball but Afridi is not aware that the ball is in Farooqi's hands. Looks for the second bye but Fazalhaq does not want to throw the ball, it seems. Indicates to Afridi that he will hit the stumps down but does not throw. The crowd likes that. It will be a bye to end the innings and PAKISTAN FINISH ON 141/8!

Commentary.Commentary: The two squads disperse and the playing XI of Afghanistan gets into a huddle. Skipper Rashid Khan, PLAYING HIS 100TH T20I, is giving some words of wisdom to his group. The umpires make their way out to the middle and now, the Afghans disperse. From the Pakistan dressing room, their two openers step down - Sahibzada Farhan and Saim Ayub. It will be Fazalhaq Farooqi to start things off, with Farhan on strike. A slip in place. Here we go!

Time now for the national anthems. It will be Pakistan's first, followed by that of Afghanistan. Right, the anthems have been sung and it is time now for the action to begin. The number 6 has a bit of a significance tonight. 6 games prior to the final, have all been won batting first in this tournament. Will game 7 have any change? Also, Afghanistan have made 6 CHANGES to their playing XI from their last game against the UAE. Understandably, having already qualified for the final before that match, the Afghans took it as an opportunity to test the bench, but sometimes, so many changes can dent your momentum. The Men In Blue will hope that is not the case.
PITCH REPORT - It is the same pitch which has been used before and has a tuft of grass, says Ramiz Raja on air. Believes that 170 could be a par total in the first innings.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran, Sediqullah Atal (In place of Sharafuddin Ashraf), Darwish Rasooli (In place of Mohammad Ishaq), Karim Janat, Azmatullah Omarzai, Rashid Khan (C) (In place of Abdullah Ahmadzai), Mohammad Nabi (In place of Gulbadin Naib), Allah Mohammad (In place of Fareed Ahmad), Noor Ahmad and Fazalhaq Farooqi (In place of Mujeeb Ur Rahman).

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Sahibzada Farhan, Saim Ayub, Fakhar Zaman, Salman Agha (C), Hasan Nawaz, Mohammad Nawaz, Mohammad Haris (WK), Faheem Ashraf, Shaheen Afridi, Sufiyan Muqeem (In place of Salman Mirza) and Abrar Ahmed.
TOSS - The coin lands in favour of Salman Agha and Pakistan have elected to BAT first.

The surface in Sharjah has shown its two-paced nature, offering some bounce for the fast bowlers early on before it settles down and slows as the game progresses. This brings the spinners into play, making batting in the second innings trickier and forcing teams to work hard for runs. A total above 170 can be considered highly competitive here, as chasing under these conditions is never straightforward.

Afghanistan have proven they’re no longer just dark horses but a genuine force capable of beating top sides, having won three of their last five T20Is against Pakistan, including two right here in Sharjah where they know the conditions inside out. Ibrahim Zadran and Sediqullah Atal have been key at the top, providing stability and aggression, while their middle-order hitters add plenty of firepower. Rashid Khan, who became the highest wicket-taker in T20Is during this series, remains their biggest match-winner, and their lethal spin attack, blending youth and experience, have already caused Pakistan problems. With their trademark energy and fearlessness, Afghanistan will be eager to break their finals jinx and take a defining step forward in their cricketing journey. If they need an additional piece of motivation, tonight will mark RASHID'S 100TH T20I - the third player from Afghanistan to achieve this feat after Mohammad Nabi and Najibullah Zadran!

Pakistan may have stumbled against Afghanistan earlier in the tournament, but they have looked the most complete side overall, and their experience of playing and winning big finals gives them a slight edge. Fakhar Zaman’s timely return to form in the previous game is a huge boost, while Saim Ayub’s explosive starts and a reliable middle order have kept their batting in good shape. Their bowling has been just as impressive, with Faheem Ashraf stepping up brilliantly to complement the strike bowlers who have been rotated nicely and Mohammad Nawaz leading the spin department with control and guile. With a trophy on the line and the Asia Cup around the corner, Pakistan will be hungry to seize this chance and make a strong statement.

Hello and a warm welcome to the grand finale of the UAE Tri-Nation Series! After a few thrilling matches over the past week, it all comes down to this blockbuster clash as fierce Asian rivals Pakistan and Afghanistan battle for bragging rights and momentum ahead of the Asia Cup. The home fans may be disappointed with UAE missing out, but this decider promises plenty of drama, with both teams having claimed a win each earlier in the series, setting the stage for a cracking contest.
... MATCH DAY ...

The T20I Tri-Series in UAE, 2025 has been a high-stakes, closely fought affair, and it all culminates in a thrilling final between two familiar foes - Pakistan and Afghanistan. The two teams have already faced off twice in the series, with each securing a victory, setting the stage for a dramatic decider at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium. Pakistan comes into the final with a strong record in the tournament, having won three of their four round-robin matches. Their journey to the final has been marked by some standout individual performances. Opener Fakhar Zaman, who had been in a lean patch, rediscovered his form with a magnificent unbeaten 77 against the UAE, while Mohammad Nawaz's crucial lower-order hitting has provided impetus to their innings. With the ball, the young leg-spinner Abrar Ahmed has been a revelation, and the pace duo of Haris Rauf and Shaheen Afridi provides a potent threat. However, the batting lineup has shown some signs of fragility, with the top order struggling to convert starts in some games. Captain Salman Agha will be looking for a more consistent performance from his batters in the high-pressure final. Afghanistan, on the other hand, have been equally impressive, also securing three wins from their four matches. Their strength lies in a balanced lineup and some explosive batting at the top. The opening pair of Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran has been in sensational form, providing solid platforms for their team to build on. Ibrahim Zadran has been a standout performer with consecutive half-centuries, and he will be a key wicket for Pakistan. Their spin attack, led by the world-class Rashid Khan and supported by Mohammad Nabi and Noor Ahmad, has been instrumental in choking opposition batsmen, as was evident in their previous win against Pakistan. The spin trio's ability to control the middle overs will be a significant factor in the final. With both teams coming into the final having secured wins in their last round-robin matches against the UAE, momentum is on their side. The final promises to be an intense battle between Pakistan's powerful batting and pace attack and Afghanistan's in-form top order and world-class spin. The stakes are high, and cricket fans can expect a captivating and closely contested finale to the Tri-Series.
